title: stack and grid nodes place their children from measured sizes
body:
Every node is placed by `at`: two numbers in its group's coordinates, or a named thing's corner plus an offset. `key-schemes.acre` places its sections at `at 0 790`, `at 0 1090`, `at 0 1520` and so on. Growing one section means moving every one after it by hand.

## Proposal

- `stack { direction down; gap N; align left; ... }` places each child after the one before, down or across, with a gap.
- `grid { columns N; gap X Y; ... }` places children in cells of a grid, each cell as large as its row's tallest and its column's widest child.
- Both measure their children: shapes and rows by their geometry, text by the shaping issue's measure, panels and nested stacks by their contents.
- A child's own `at` inside a stack or grid becomes an offset from its place.

## Open

- How `at NAME dx dy` resolves when the named thing sits inside a stack: the builder has to lay out before it resolves names, so name resolution moves after layout.
